brief: The census throws away most of what it computes. `summarize()` in `.claude/skills/grow-courtyard/census.mjs` folds `c.scalars`, `c.tiles`, `c.life`, `c.structure` and `c.planting.bySpecies` — and silently drops the rest of `planting`: `planted`, `blooming`, `daisies`, `mossy`, `matureTrees`, `worn`, `harvested` and `produce`. `mossy` was added by #103 precisely so the census could see the moss, and at #114 it moved 265 -> 358 while the gate printed 'planting: unchanged'. Fold the remaining `planting` fields into the summary as their own group and surface them in the report. Then run the census twice on HEAD and record what the NEW fields' own churn is, so the next brief that leans on one knows its noise floor. This is an instrument change: nothing in `courtyard.html` should differ. It reshapes the baseline, so re-pin with `--save-baseline` and say so in the ledger entry. It is first in the queue so that b116's re-pin is the only other one this batch needs.
successLooksLike: `node census.mjs` prints mossy, worn, daisies, matureTrees and harvested with deltas, and the entry quotes each new field's HEAD-against-HEAD spread so it is usable as evidence rather than decoration.
avoid: Do not add fields to `__census()` — it already computes everything you need. Do not widen the CORE collapse-gate list; a noisy new field in CORE turns the gate into a coin flip. Do not touch courtyard.html.
